help:
Selects where the drive gets its speed reference. F7 scales the analog and pulse inputs.

0 — Keypad potentiometer
1 — Digital setting F0.01 from the keypad
2 — UP/DOWN inputs, with the reference retained
3 — RS-485, initial reference from F0.01
4 — VCI voltage input, 0–10 V
5 — CCI voltage or current input, 0–10 V or 4–20 mA, set by the V/A switch
6 — Reserved
7 — Pulse frequency on X5 (F5.04 = 38, F7.13–F7.17)
8 — Combined reference (F2.09)
9 — UP/DOWN inputs without retention, starting at F0.01
10 — RS-485, with the reference retained at power-off
11 — Pulse width (PWM), scaled by F7.08–F7.12
Sets the initial reference for digital keypad control and the RS-485 mode F0.00 = 3. It also supplies the initial value for UP/DOWN without retention (F0.00 = 9).

Selects who can start and stop the drive. With terminal or RS-485 commands, the selected mode also determines whether keypad STOP is active.

0 — Keypad
1 — Terminals, keypad STOP disabled
2 — Terminals, keypad STOP enabled
3 — RS-485, keypad STOP disabled
4 — RS-485, keypad STOP enabled

Read the digits from right to left.
Units — 0 forward, 1 reverse (keypad and RS-485).
Tens — 0 permit reverse, 1 inhibit reverse (all command sources).
Hundreds — 0 REV key, 1 JOG key.
note: The table in §5.2 and the description in §6.1 print different factory settings. The editor displays the profile's 000.

help:
Selects the shape of the output frequency ramp.

0 — Linear ramp
1 — S-curve (F0.05 and F0.06)
Percentage of the ramp spent increasing the slope from zero in S-curve mode. F0.05 + F0.06 must be at most 90%.
Percentage of the S-curve ramp with constant slope. The remaining time is used for the final transition to zero slope. F0.05 + F0.06 must be at most 90%.
note: §5.2 gives a 70% upper limit, while §6.1 gives 80%. The profile uses the limit from §5.2.

help:
Sets the unit for ramp sets 1–7. Jog ramps are set in seconds and PLC step duration has its own unit in F4.00.

0 — Seconds
1 — Minutes
Ramp set 1. Time from 0 Hz to the upper frequency limit F0.10. The unit comes from F0.07.
Ramp set 1. Time from the upper frequency limit F0.10 to 0 Hz. The unit comes from F0.07.
Caps the output frequency and serves as the reference for acceleration and deceleration times.
If the requested frequency falls below this threshold, F0.12 determines how the drive responds.

Sets the response when the frequency reference is below F0.11.

0 — Run at F0.11
1 — Reduce output frequency to 0 Hz

Selects how the drive boosts motor voltage at low frequency.

0 — Fixed boost set by F0.14
1 — Automatic boost based on motor current
Sets the low-frequency voltage boost used to improve starting torque. Excessive boost can cause heating or overcurrent.

Sets the relationship between output voltage and frequency. In user-defined mode, F2.37–F2.44 hold the curve coordinates.

0 — Constant torque
1 — Variable torque, power law 2.0
2 — Variable torque, power law 1.7
3 — Variable torque, power law 1.2
4 — User-defined V/F curve

Selects the sequence after a run command.

0 — Start at F1.01 and hold it for F1.02
1 — DC brake using F1.03/F1.04, then start
2 — Reserved
The first output frequency after start. The lower operating limit F0.11 does not constrain it.
Time spent at F1.01 before the drive continues accelerating.
Sets the DC braking voltage for the zero-frequency braking function. F1.00 = 1 also uses this value for braking before starting.
Sets the duration of the DC braking associated with F1.03. Stop-command braking is set separately in F1.06–F1.08.

Defines what happens when a stop command is received.

0 — Ramp down to 0 Hz
1 — Coast with the drive output switched off
2 — Ramp down to F1.06, then apply DC braking

description: DC braking start frequency at stop
help: When F1.05 = 2, DC braking begins as the output frequency falls to this value.
Sets DC braking duration when F1.05 = 2. A setting of 0 skips the DC braking phase.
DC braking voltage as a percentage of the drive's rated input voltage.
A longer time constant smooths noisy analog signals and slows the response. §6.3 specifies a value above the sampling period F3.11.
Time the drive holds zero output frequency during a forward-to-reverse or reverse-to-forward transition.

Adjusts output voltage based on motor current under steady, light load.

0 — Disabled
1 — Enabled

Keeps output voltage stable when the input voltage varies.

0 — Disabled
1 — Enabled throughout operation
2 — Enabled except during deceleration
Compensates the induction motor's speed drop as load increases by adjusting output frequency. 0 disables compensation.
Sets the inverter switching frequency. Higher settings typically reduce audible motor noise but increase switching losses. Check the model limits in Table 6-1.
Target frequency while a JOG command is active. JOG uses the separate ramps F2.07 and F2.08.

Deceleration time in JOG, specified in seconds for a change from F0.10 to 0 Hz.

Upper setpoint used to scale the feedback curve. F3.07 defines the matching feedback value.

Sets how strongly the controller responds to the current error. A high gain can cause oscillations.
Sets how strongly accumulated error acts to remove a persistent offset.
Sets the response to the rate of change of error. 0 removes the derivative contribution.
Interval between feedback samples and PID updates.
Error allowed as a percentage of the setpoint. In standard PID mode, the drive holds its output when the error is within this band.
§6.4 specifies that integration acts when both setpoint and feedback are at or below this threshold.
The drive ramps to this frequency before starting closed-loop regulation. Holding time is set by F3.15.
Time spent at F3.14 before the controller takes over. Set both F3.14 and F3.15 to zero to skip the preset stage.
Low frequency threshold for going to sleep. F3.18 determines how long the sleep condition must persist.
note: §6.4 interchanges F3.16 and F3.17 in the headings. The profile follows the assignment in the §5.2 table.

help: Threshold for returning to operation from sleep. F3.19 determines how long the wake-up condition must persist.

help: Delay before the drive enters sleep while the sleep condition persists.
